segments.text: The best short clip starts with one clear idea.
Before you edit anything, ask yourself what the viewer will learn, feel, or want to share.
Look for a surprising statement, a useful answer, or a story with a turning point.
Give the idea enough room to make sense.
A complete thought will always work better than a random sentence taken out of context.
Your opening seconds need to earn attention.
Start close to the interesting moment, remove the long introduction, and keep the strongest sentence near the beginning.
Then give the viewer a reason to stay.
A simple question can create curiosity, but the rest of the clip must deliver the answer.
Cut the pauses that slow the story down, while keeping the speaker's voice natural.
Finish your clip so it is easy to watch on a phone.
Use a vertical frame, keep the important subject in view, and add readable captions with strong contrast.
Check every caption against the original audio.
Choose a thumbnail that shows the idea clearly, with only a few words.
Watch the whole export before sharing it.
Strong short videos are clear, useful, and complete.
